# Agent Team Console

Read-only Agent Teams dashboard for the DeepSeek Harness Web UI (`dsh-agent-team-console`): a
projec

t-scoped, card-grid view of every team, with a top-down pixel-art agent flow graph and rounds /
toke
n / working-time statistics in one first-class main panel.

Repository: <https://github.com/kkomia/dsh-agent-team-console>

## Why this plugin
The official experimental Agent Teams Web UI (`@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-client-ui-agent-team`)

adds a compact roster and task-board action to the conversation header. That is convenient for a
qui
ck check while you are inside the Lead conversation, but it is not a page of its own.

Agent Team Console keeps the same read-only contract and adds a sidebar entry plus a full main
panel
for people who keep a team running for a long stretch:
[该节后续省略]
## Requirements and compatibility
- **DSH Web UI** in the desktop app or a Web profile. The plugin was developed and tested against DS

H
`0.2.1-rc.2`; `package.json` declares `engines.dsh` as `>=0.2.1-rc.2 <0.3.0-0`, which also exclude

s
0.3.0 prereleases.
- **The official experimental Agent Teams bundle must be mounted in the same pr

ofile.** This plugin
visualizes teams that already exist; it does not provide the Agent Teams servic

e itself. Without
that service the panel shows a clear "not mounted" notice instead of failing.
- **

Optional session projections.** Rounds, token usage, and working / idle times come from the stock
DS

H `sessionStats` and `tokenUsage` projections. They are optional: without them the panel still
rende

rs the graph and shows dashes for statistics.
- **A Web-capable profile.** The install examples belo

w use the `desktop` profile; replace `desktop`
with your own Web profile name (`web`, and so on) if

it differs.
- **No separate Node.js installation is needed to use the plugin.** Node.js 22.19 or new

er is only
needed to run the tests in this repository.
## Read-only and privacy
Agent Team Console is deliberately conservative:
- **One read-only route.** The host half serves exactly `GET /api/team-console/snapshot`; for admitt

ed
requests, any other path returns a JSON 404. No POST, PUT, PATCH, or DELETE route exists, and the

handler never reads the request body.
- **No mutations.** Neither half calls a create, update, dele

te, claim, complete, spawn, or interrupt
operation on a team, member, task, or session service.
- **

No external network access.** The panel fetches a relative, same-origin URL. There is no CDN, no
rem

ote font or image, no telemetry, and no analytics call.
- **No disk access and no timers on the host

.** The host half keeps no mutable module state and
touches no files; every request rebuilds a snaps

hot from live read-only service reads.
- **Minimal client dependencies.** The browser bundle require

s only `react` from the host module
system; it imports no `@deepseek-ai/*` package and no third-part

y bundle.
- **Data stays local.** The snapshot is assembled from data the Web UI already holds (name

s, roles,
statuses, task text) and is served by the local Harness Web server, typically on a loopbac

k
address, only to same-origin clients of your own instance.
- **Admission matches the Web UI.** Whe

n the host mounts the DSH `connection` service, the route asks
it to admit every request before runn

ing any route logic: a request that fails the Host/Origin fence
or the browser-session check receive

s a JSON `401` (`unauthorized`) or `403` (`forbidden`) response
and is rejected exactly like any oth

er Web UI request. An authenticated same-origin browser fetch is
admitted. If a host does not mount

that service, the route leaves admission to the deployment's own
access control.
- **Bounded payload

s.** Text fields are capped (task descriptions at 2000 characters, activity labels
at 200 characters
); the snapshot is JSON-safe by construction.
## Limitations
- **Unofficial and experimental.** This is a community plugin built on the experimental Agent Teams

services, which may change between DSH versions. The declared compatibility range is
`>=0.2.1-rc.2 <

0.3.0-0`.
- **Polling, not push.** Data can be up to about 2 seconds old, and the host rebuilds the

snapshot for
every request. Polling pauses while the tab is hidden.
- **Only real teams are listed.*

* A team appears when it has more than one member or at least one
shared task; an ordinary single-ag

ent Lead session is not listed.
- **The project filter is client-side.** It is not persisted and is

hidden when only one project has
live teams. Teams whose project cannot be resolved appear under "Al

l projects" only and show the
"No project" label.
- **One card expands at a time.** The workspace gr

id is an accordion: the default expanded card is the
first active team, an explicit collapse is reme

mbered across polls, and switching cards collapses
the previous one.
- **Stats are best effort.** Tu

rns, steps, token usage, and working / idle times come from the
optional session projections; when t

hey are unavailable the host emits nulls and the graph and
detail card show dashes. Stats never trig

ger a session-log scan.
- **Activity is API-only.** The snapshot still carries the bounded activity

list (at most 40 entries
per team) for API consumers, but the panel does not render it.
- **Message

links are bounded.** Message edges aggregate the newest 1000 events of each member's
session log (Le

ad included) for live `agent-message` deliveries, plus the newest 2000 Lead-session
events for legac

y `team/message/queued` records. Older traffic is not observed; the live source
counts only deliveri

es that reached a member session, while legacy queued records are counted as
recorded. Only structur

al Lead links and observed message edges are represented (no tool-call or
task-dependency graph).
-
**The graph shows up to 8 members.** Larger teams show a "+N" node in the last row instead of every

member; teammates are grouped into one row for up to 5 and two balanced rows beyond that.
